name: Foum El Oued Beach
hero_subtitle: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic: a long Blue Flag sandy coastline, ocean breezes, and golden sunsets just 25 km from Laâyoune.

overview.title: The Atlantic Escape of the Moroccan Sahara
overview.p1: Foum El Oued Beach is the main seaside outlet for Laâyoune residents and visitors. Stretching over seven kilometres of fine Atlantic sand, this Blue Flag beach (awarded for many consecutive years) combines clean waters, a landscaped promenade, and the unique landscape of desert dunes meeting the ocean.
overview.p2: Located about 25 kilometres southwest of the city centre, it is easily reached by grand taxi or private car in around 20–25 minutes. The beach offers lifeguard zones in summer, parking, sanitary facilities, and a relaxed family atmosphere.
overview.p3: Whether you come for a quiet morning walk, kitesurfing when the wind picks up, or a sunset tea by the water, Foum El Oued delivers one of the most authentic coastal experiences in southern Morocco.

moods.title: Experiencing Foum El Oued Through the Day
moods.subtitle: The beach changes character from morning calm to lively afternoons and peaceful evenings.

1.title: Quiet, Fresh & Ideal for Walks
1.desc: Early morning is the best time for peaceful walks, photography of the empty shoreline, and enjoying cooler temperatures before the day warms up. Perfect for runners and those seeking solitude.

2.title: Sun, Swimming & Water Sports
2.desc: From late morning the beach fills with families and locals. Lifeguards are present in season. The steady wind makes it popular for kitesurf and windsurf. Bring strong sunscreen and a hat.

3.title: Golden Light & Ocean Breeze
3.desc: Late afternoon into evening brings the most beautiful light and cooler air. Many stay for sunset, then enjoy a simple seafood snack or tea before heading back to the city.

food.title: What to Eat Near Foum El Oued
food.p1: While the beach itself is more about nature than restaurants, several simple eateries and seasonal stands offer fresh Atlantic seafood and drinks.
food.li1: Grilled sardines and fresh fish, often prepared on the spot near the parking or promenade.
food.li2: Fried calamari and simple seafood platters with lemon and local bread.
food.li3: Fresh fruit juices and soft drinks from kiosks along the corniche.
food.li4: Mint tea or Sahrawi Atay to enjoy while watching the waves.
food.li5: For a bigger meal, combine the beach visit with lunch at El Marsa Port (a short drive away).
food.p2: Many visitors prefer to bring a picnic or return to Laâyoune for more restaurant options after the beach.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Foum El Oued Beach

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Grand taxis leave regularly from Laâyoune city centre (near Place Mechouar or the main taxi ranks). The ride takes 20–25 minutes and costs a modest fixed fare. Private taxis and rental cars are also easy options.

2.title: Swimming & Safety
2.desc: The Atlantic can have strong currents and waves. Swim only in supervised zones when lifeguards are present. Always check local flags and conditions. Children should be closely supervised.

3.title: What to Bring
3.desc: Strong sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, water, and a light jacket for the evening breeze. The sand can get hot in summer. Facilities include parking, toilets, and basic showers in season.

gyg.subtitle: Local guides can arrange half-day or full-day trips including the beach, port, and desert landscapes.

t2.title: Laâyoune Coast & Dunes Experience
t2.desc: Beach time, short dune walk, and Sahrawi tea with ocean views.

t3.title: Family Beach Day from Laâyoune
t3.desc: Easy transfer, time on the sand, and simple facilities suitable for children.

q1.question: Is Foum El Oued Beach free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes, the beach is completely free and open to the public year-round. Parking is also free or very inexpensive.

q2.question: How far is the beach from Laâyoune city centre?
q2.answer: Approximately 25 kilometres (about 20–25 minutes by taxi or car).

q3.question: Is it safe to swim at Foum El Oued?
q3.answer: Swimming is possible in designated areas, especially in summer when lifeguards are present. The Atlantic can have strong currents, so always follow local advice and flags.

q4.question: What is the best time of year to visit?
q4.answer: October to April for pleasant temperatures. Summer (June–September) is popular with locals escaping the heat but can be hotter and busier.

q5.question: Are there restaurants and facilities on the beach?
q5.answer: Basic facilities (toilets, showers in season, parking) and simple seafood stands are available. For a wider choice of restaurants, head to El Marsa Port or back to the city.
